content: Welcome to my first self-built site. A place for my thoughts and notes across all fields. It’s a blank slate for now, but soon it will be filled with a harvest of posts.

I took a day trip to Rottnest Island on January 11th, and it was truly a wonderful experience.
Before I go # Since most people only spend a day on Rottnest Island, I did some research beforehand and looked up lots of travel tips to make the most of my trip. It definitely saved me both time and money.
Booking Ferry return tickets(and get discount) # There are two main ferry companies to Rottnest Island: Rottnest Express and Sealink. I went with Rottnest Express this time. The main reason I chose them was the discount codes you can sometimes find on promotional flyers around Perth city centre. I got the code while browsing tips on Rednote, another traveler had kindly shared it from a promotional flyer few days earlier, so I used it.
Typically, ferry tickets are usually quite expensive during the Christmas to mid-January peak season, as they also include the mandatory island admission fee. However, with the discount code, my total round trip cost was just under A$90!
Transportation on Rottnest Island # There are two main ways of exploring around the island, by bike or by tourist bus. The bus runs roughly every 20 minutes and stops at all the major attractions. Many travelers’ posts mentioned that the bus service ends around 3-4pm, so it is important to keep an eye on the time. If you are still exploring the further parts of the island in the late afternoon, make sure to check the last bus departure so you don’t get stranded.
If you prefer more freedom to enjoy the scenery, renting a bike is the way to go. You can book your bike online in advance. Although there is only one bike rental shop on the island， they have a massive fleet, so you don’t need to worry about them running out. Just make sure to check the bike’s condition before setting off.
However, if you want an E-bike, you must act fast. They are in high demand due to the hilly terrain. Even though I tried booking two days in advance, all the E-bikes were already gone. Therefore, I highly recommend reserving your E-bike a few days (or even a week) in advance, if you want to save your energy and have a more relaxed ride. Otherwise, be prepared for a serious workout!
But here is a little secret: if you arrive on the island early enough, you might still get lucky even if they are sold out online. I arrived on the island around 8am. Since I got there early, I went straight to the bike rental counter to ask if there were any e-bikes left. And as it turned out, a fresh batch of E-bikes had just been charged and released.
Rottnest Express also offers bike rentals during the booking process on their website. However, I wasn’t sure if they had their own fleet or were partnering with the island’s rental warehouse. Since I didn’t see an E-bike option there at the time, I held off on booking.
Someone might feel that using an E-bike for island cycling isn’t CHALLENGING enough, but for me, this trip was all about vacation vibes. I just wanted to relax and take in the scenery.
In addition, another most important thing you need to know is taking care yourself during the bike trip. This is a real lesson I learned the hard way:
No matter what kind of bike you’re riding, sitting on the saddle for a long time can really take a toll on your body. I cycled from the morning until around 2pm that day, and towards the end, I was basically dealing with constant saddle pain. Later I got it was caused by prolonged pressure on the soft tissue under the sitting bones.
So I strongly recommend taking regular breaks during your ride and standing up to move around whenever possible. My case wasn’t too serious that went away after I got back to the hotel in the evening. But I still want to remind everyone: don’t let seat pain ruin an otherwise amazing scenery experience.
The scenery around the island # Before my trip, I didn’t do much research on the island’s attractions. I wanted to simply enjoy cycling around the island at my own pace. Even without a plan, the scenery along the coastal roads was absolutely stunning. The route takes you past countless beautiful beaches, and many of the bus stops are located at excellent viewpoints where you can stop for a break and admire the views.
Some of my favourite spots were Army Jetty, Parker Point, both Salmon Bays (the larger and the little one), everything around the western island (West End), and the chain of lakes in the centre of the island.
Parker Point features a beautiful wooden boardwalk, and on a clear day you can even see the Perth skyline in the distance.The scenery around West End is incredibly open and dramatic, and the track leads the way to the westernmost point of the island. I’ve heard it’s sometimes possible to spot whales or dolphins from the shoreline there, although I wasn’t lucky enough to see either on my visit. Crocodile Rock is a good spot too.
After spending hours riding past one beautiful beach after another, you might start to feel a little beached out. That’s why I also recommend taking a detour through the island’s central salt lakes. It’s only a few kilometres from the main settlement, and you’ll discover a completely different side of the island with peaceful lakes and quiet atmosphere.
I didn’t visit Pink Lake. I wasn’t quite sure how to fit Pink Lake into my cycling route, as it’s located in the middle of the island. I don’t want to ride an extra distance just to get there then continue my loop around the island. Besides, Pink Lake isn’t always pink. It depends on the weather and the lighting conditions. So I don’t think it is a must-see especially you are short on time. The other lakes around the island are well worth a visit too. They’re peaceful, and you even have a good chance of spotting Quokkas along the way.
title: A day trip in Rottnest Island
